route: Structural correspondence between the .sav's labelled constructs and the S1 Appendix questionnaire order (SKILL.md Step 5b route 2/5 variant)
evidence: In the same .sav, every construct that DOES carry variable labels matches the S1 Appendix item at exactly its own within-construct position: US1/US2/US3 = appendix items 13/14/15, TTF1/TTF2/TTF3 = 16/17/18, PI1-PI4 = 19-22 and PI6-PI10 = 24-28, and the excluded column PI5_del is labelled 'Online learning enhances my academic effectiveness.' = appendix item 23, i.e. the 5th Performance Impact item. That is 16/16 exact matches plus the gap column landing on its own number, establishing that the numeric suffix indexes the construct's questionnaire order and that dropped numbers leave a hole rather than shifting later items. Applying the same rule, CA1/CA2/CA4/CA6 = appendix items 29/30/32/34. Live item stats are consistent (all four means 4.66-4.77, sd ~1.4, no discriminating signal available), so the structural route rather than statistics carries the check.

route: structural: within-construct position convention proven on labelled sibling columns (+ item means)
evidence: The .sav labels 15 sibling columns whose codes can be checked against the same S1 Appendix: US1/US2/US3 = appendix User Satisfaction rows 1/2/3, TTF1/TTF2/TTF3 = Task Technology Fit rows 1/2/3, PI1..PI10 = Performance Impact rows 1..10 including the dropped PI5_del labelled 'Online learning enhances my academic effectiveness.' = that block's 5th row, and AU1/AU2 = Actual Usage rows 1/2. Zero exceptions in 18 labelled columns, so code number = position within its construct block; the IF codes preserve the gaps at IF3 and IF11 (not renumbered after those items were dropped), so IFn = appendix IF row n. Corroborating magnitude check: live IF item means 4.7-5.1 average 4.85, matching the paper's Table 3 Institutional Factors mean of 4.85 (SD 1.4, N=404). No per-item statistics are published for IF, so no route-1 item-level discrimination is available.

route: route 6 attempted (keying polarity) - UNAVAILABLE; route 7 marker item + alpha match only
evidence: Polarity route dead: all 45 inter-item correlations are positive (+0.12 to +0.63) and every item-total is positive, i.e. the five negatively worded items are stored already reversed, so no sign pattern distinguishes them. An exhaustive search over all 252 possible 5-item subsets found NO reverse-wording method factor either (canonical negative set {2,5,6,8,9}: mean within-group r = 0.263/0.304, mean cross-group r = 0.315 -- no separation). Remaining, weak, corroboration: (a) RSES8 has the lowest mean of the ten (1.53 of 3, next lowest 1.70), matching the well-documented marker behaviour of RSES item 8 ('I wish I could have more respect for myself'); (b) computed Cronbach alpha = 0.805 matches the paper's reported RSES alpha of 0.81 exactly, confirming the block is the RSES; (c) RSES1 has the highest mean (2.24), as expected for item 1. None of this rules out a permuted administration order of the kind found in bakker_2020_rses. ORCHESTRATOR ADDITION 2026-08-18: position 8 now has positive support. RSES8 has both the lowest mean (1.53) and the lowest item-rest correlation (0.36 vs 0.40-0.57 for the rest), which is the known signature of Rosenberg item 8 ('I wish I could have more respect for myself'), the scale's classic misfitting item; the same item showed the same signature at position 8 in bang_2023_self_esteem, and in the permuted bakker_2020_rses file position 8 was one of the three columns whose name and label agreed. Alpha 0.805 vs the paper's 0.81. Positions 1-7, 9 and 10 remain unconfirmed - any permutation among them is consistent with everything observable. Shipped on Ben's call with a callout saying so.

route: route 6 (reverse-item method factor, exhaustive subset search) + route 1 (per-item means vs an independent Czech SOC-13 sample)
evidence: (1) Reverse-item method factor: scoring every one of the 1287 possible 5-item subsets of soc1..soc13 by (mean within-group r) minus (mean cross-group r), the canonical SOC-13 reverse set {1,2,3,7,10} ranks FIRST of 1287 (0.126; runner-up {1,2,3,10,13} = 0.107). Within-group r 0.236/0.279 vs cross-group 0.142. (2) Per-item means match an independent Czech SOC-13 sample (Research Square rs-2723276, N=498) item-for-item: theirs 5.01/3.73/3.96/5.25/4.76/4.97/4.89/4.67/4.27/4.21/4.49/4.98/4.99 vs ours 5.03/3.66/4.19/5.85/5.16/5.09/5.16/4.45/4.36/4.51/4.47/5.37/4.47, Pearson r = 0.87, mean absolute difference 0.25, with item 2 the distinct minimum (~3.7) in both. (3) That study's known item-2/item-3 residual covariance reproduces here as the largest off-diagonal correlation of the reverse block (r = 0.60). All items positively keyed => data stored already reverse-scored, which is how the shipped anchors were oriented.

route: route 5 (subscale block structure) + item-number cross-source confirmation
evidence: mapping_structure.R on the GAI's published 3-factor item assignment (cognitive 1,2,3,5,8,9,11,14,16,17,19; arousal 4,6,10,13,20; somatic 7,12,15,18) gives 15/20 items loading strongest on their hypothesised subscale. All three purely-somatic items 7,12,18 are own-best (mean r .49/.48/.45 vs rivals), which is the discriminating block; the 5 misses (gai3,6,8,9 cognitive-vs-arousal, gai15 somatic-vs-arousal) are all near-ties (e.g. gai8 own .42 vs rival .43, gai9 .42 vs .42) between facets known to be near-collinear under the GAI's strong general factor, so a low count here is underpowered rather than evidence against the mapping. Independent confirmation that Pachana Table 2's listing order IS final items 1-20: PMC6624870 Table 2 prints explicit item numbers 1-20 against identical English texts and agrees on all 20. Direction of resp verified separately: all 20 item-rest r positive (+0.39..+0.70), means 0.11-0.34 => 1=Agree. Not fully VERIFIED because no per-item statistics for this Czech sample are published anywhere to match against.

route: 6+7+8 (keying polarity, marker items, semantic coherence of endorsement rates)
evidence: Routes 6 (keying polarity) + 7 (marker items) + 8 (semantic coherence). Polarity: all 15 corrected item-total rs positive (gds6 .25, gds10 .30, gds11 .33, gds15 .42 lowest; gds3 .63, gds12 .61 highest) -> items consistently keyed, i.e. stored pre-scored, and the shipped per-item option direction follows that. Direction fixed by total score: M=3.44 (SD 3.40), 72.9% in the paper's 0-4 normal band, 4.4% at 12-15; the reversed reading would give M=11.6 (severe) for the average community-dwelling 60+ respondent. Numbering pinned by the canonical GDS-15 signature: the three weakest item-total items are exactly gds6 ('afraid something bad will happen', .25), gds10 ('problems with memory', .30) and gds11 ('wonderful to be alive', .33), the items the GDS-15 literature reports as weakest; and endorsement ordering is semantically coherent -- rarest are gds14 hopeless (.092) and gds1 not satisfied with life (.096), most common gds6 (.458) and gds13 not full of energy (.446). No per-item statistics are published in the paper, so item-by-item confirmation within the polarity class is not possible: PARTIAL.

Route 6 (keying polarity) + route 8 (semantic coherence). (a) Reversal status: raw column sum reproduces the paper's reported LSITA total exactly (36.30/8.68/12-62 vs published 36.34/8.66/12-62) and all 66 inter-item r are positive (.12-.62), so items 2/4/5/6 are stored already reversed; scale direction confirmed against sibling scales in the same file (r with GDS-15 sum +0.66, GAI +0.31, RSES -0.49, SOC-13 -0.54, age +0.23, all matching the paper's published signs and magnitudes). (b) Reverse set identified from the data independently: the ratio count(resp=3) / mean(count(2),count(4)) is 0.42/0.49/0.54/0.56 for items 2/6/4/5 and 0.76-1.41 for the other eight -- the four deepest are exactly the canonical reverse set (1-in-495 by chance). (c) Reverse-worded method factor: mean within-block r among {2,4,5,6} = 0.47 vs cross-block 0.34, and each of the four has within > cross. (d) Endorsement ordering is semantically coherent: strongest disagreement with the most extreme negative statement (item 2 'dreariest time', raw mean 4.42) down to the mildest (item 5 'could be happier', 3.44); strongest agreement with 'looking back I am well satisfied' (2.53), weakest with 'Everything is just great' (3.72). PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED: order WITHIN each polarity class rests on canonical item numbering -- the only per-item statistics for this sample are in the paywalled companion validation paper (10.1111/opn.12541), so route 1 was unavailable.
